title: Final CAD/BIM feasibility: adapter replacement + end-to-end workflow (engine-independent canonical semantics)
objective: Earn the final CAD/BIM feasibility decision with reproducible evidence that the frozen adapter boundary is real, replaceable, and supports the defining ConstructionOS workflow. Prove (1) a second/reference geometry adapter (pure TypeScript, no FreeCAD/OCCT/IfcOpenShell anywhere in its dependency graph) satisfies the same stable CAD/BIM contracts and produces semantically equivalent results; (2) the Construction Graph and the downstream domain contracts consume canonical identities — engine GlobalIds are provenance only, so replacing the engine does not change canonical ConstructionOS semantics (identities, document content, graph events, downstream structure identical; values within declared tolerances); and (3) the existential end-to-end chain Model change → Model version → Quantity delta → Estimate impact → Affected RFQ → Commercial impact, deterministic and replayable, with Web/Electron semantic parity through the shared App API, exact tolerances, provenance and uncertainty labels. Research/evidence only: no architecture change, no APPROVED/VERIFIED claim by implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A second/reference geometry adapter (app/src/adapters/reference — pure TypeScript analytic solid geometry, engine-free by construction and by static LOCK-018 checks) implements the byte-unchanged GeometryEngineAdapter contract with the optional MeshProvider/GeometryMetadataProvider capabilities and the same typed engine_malformed_input failure surface as the OCCT adapter.

The reference adapter passes the SAME representative geometry workflow as the OCCT adapter (one element per descriptor vocabulary node: box, cylinder+direction, transform, disjoint fuse, axis-aligned cut): real-engine and reference results agree within declared tolerances (volume 1e-6 relative — measured max 4.16e-9 on the corpus; bbox 0.02 absolute per the OCCT tolerance-inclusive Bnd_Box — measured max 3.6e-4), while meshTokens remain engine-local by design.

Replacing the engine behind the frozen boundary changes NOTHING canonical: identical document content hash, identical revision history, byte-identical Construction Graph event streams (identical events_hash), identical downstream identities (quantity ids, cost item ids, estimate ids, RFQ package ids, graph node ids, downstream event ids); measured values agree within the declared tolerances; a document saved by one engine is opened and consumed by the other with identical identities.

Construction Graph mappings remain stable when engine GlobalIds change: the element↔graph-node identity mapping is identical across provenance variants (occt:…, reference:…, none); graph node ids are a pure function of (document entity id, element id); engine ids appear only in provenance fields and epistemic uncertainty labels.

Downstream consumers import no FreeCAD/OCCT/IfcOpenShell internals: the impact cascade core (src/impact) is added to the LOCK-018 protected-core scan and passes; a new boundary-direction check asserts the reference adapter itself imports no engine/host module.

Model revision produces deterministic quantity/change results and downstream impact: the existential chain model.version.created → quantity.recalculate.requested → quantity.changed → estimate.recalculated → rfq.scope.impact.detected → commercial impact runs deterministically (fixed timestamps, canonical ordering, canonical-hash event ids, byte-identical events_hash across runs and across save/open), with exact analytic deltas on the corpus, causation rooted at the corresponding graph event.

A model change propagates to estimate and affected-RFQ contracts without manual re-entry (the additive impact.cascade App API query), with only the affected category packages flagged (concrete affected, steel unaffected in the corpus workflow) and the aggregate commercial impact computed from the same deterministic records.

Web and Electron produce equivalent semantic downstream results: byte-identical cascades through WebSocketTransport/WebHost and IpcTransport/ElectronHost with both the reference engine and (engine-gated) the real OCCT engine; the deployable Web host serves the full workflow from the dev server with real OCCT server-side; the deployable Electron host runs the chain through a real BrowserWindow with the reference engine bound.

Existing CAD-IMPLEMENT-001/002 tests remain green and new CAD-007 tests are reproducible in CI: the full app suite (139/139 with the pinned OCCT toolchain) runs in the new research-cad-007 workflow plus the three regression workflows unchanged; the committed evidence artifact (equivalence matrix, swap skeleton, cascade snapshot) regenerates deterministically.

Epistemic honesty throughout (LOCK-007): quantities are CALCULATED under an explicit method + declared tolerance with engine provenance; elements without a measurable descriptor and elements outside an adapter's exactness classes are recorded as UNKNOWN skips, never guessed; the rate table is a labelled demo fixture, not market data; the reference engine declines typed outside its declared exactness classes rather than approximating.
No protected architecture paths are modified (check-protected green); Architecture v1.1 remains FROZEN; no APPROVED or VERIFIED state is claimed by the implementation.
non_goals: No production commercial optimization beyond the existential contract test (Issue #32 non-goal) — the rate table is a deterministic demo fixture.
No architecture modification (Issue #32 non-goal); Architecture v1.1 remains FROZEN; no protected-path edits.
No general CSG engine: the reference adapter's boolean coverage is its declared exactness class (disjoint-AABB fuse, axis-aligned-box cut); outside it fails typed.

No production estimate/RFQ domain services: the downstream contracts + cascade are the canonical research slice proving the chain; production rate binding, bid handling and subcontractor reattribution are later work items.
No approval or verification claim: the final feasibility decision belongs to the Architect.

The authoritative scope for this record is GitHub Issue #32 + the Architect execution directive (comment 5429094699, 2026-08-26T17:58:56Z). spec/ files are untouched (protected/architecture-adjacent).

Engine provenance is document content: the CADDocument content hash legitimately includes the element's recorded engineId provenance field, so the same model recorded with different engine provenance has different version ids (and version-scoped quantity ids). This is recorded honestly in graph-identity-stability.test.ts — the INVARIANT that holds (and what Issue #32's criterion asks) is that the element↔graph-node identity mapping, event-type sequences, element projections and version-FREE downstream identities are identical across engine GlobalId variants.

meshToken and tessellation counts are engine-local viewport data, never canonical values: cross-engine equivalence covers bbox/volume (the canonical quantity surface) and all identities; tokens differing across engines is by design and asserted as such.

The deterministic demo rate table (demo-rates-2026-08, GHS, source demo-fixture) is a FIXTURE for the existential contract test — LOCK-007 provenance is recorded on every cost item; binding real market/supplier rates is a production estimate concern (data-model.md §3) outside this gate.

The reference adapter's cut/fuse coverage is the declared exactness class (plane-split cell decomposition for axis-aligned box combinations; disjoint-AABB fuse). Overlapping general booleans are declined with typed engine_error and recorded as adapter-declined UNKNOWN skips downstream — the reference engine never approximates (LOCK-007). The OCCT engine has no such restriction; the corpus for cross-engine agreement lives inside the reference exactness class by design and is labelled so.

CAD-IMPLEMENT-003's post-merge close-out PR #30 remains OPEN on GitHub (main still carries that record at PR_OPEN) — pre-existing governance debt outside this gate's scope; this record does not modify it.
